name: nice
description: The nice() system call adds the specified increment to the nice value of the calling thread, affecting its scheduling priority where a higher nice value means lower priority. The nice value is clamped to the range of -20 (high priority) to +19 (low priority). Only privileged processes can lower the nice value, though unprivileged processes may do so under certain conditions like RLIMIT_NICE.

parameters.name: inc
parameters.description: Increment value to add to the nice value of the calling thread

return_value.success: Returns the new nice value on success
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The calling process attempted to increase its priority by supplying a negative inc but has insufficient privileges

bugs: The nice value may not have its traditional effect in many circumstances due to the 'autogroup' feature introduced in Linux 2.6.38.
versions: Glibc 2.2.4 and later for POSIX conformance
